mcq.q:
Consider the following statements about the Planning Commission:
1. It was set up in 1950.
2. The Finance Minister was its Chairperson.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.why: Set up in 1950 with the Prime Minister (not the Finance Minister) as its Chairperson.

mcq.q: According to NCERT, the goals of India's five year plans were:
mcq.why: The four goals: growth, modernisation, self-reliance (the Recap says self-sufficiency) and equity.

mcq.q:
Consider the following statements about the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956:
1. It formed the basis of the First Five Year Plan.
2. It classified industries into three categories.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.why: IPR 1956 had three categories of industries, and it formed the basis of the Second Five Year Plan.

mcq.q: The Karve Committee (1955), which noted the role of small-scale industries in rural development, was also called the:
options: Industrial Licensing and Small Units Committee
mcq.why: NCERT: the Village and Small-Scale Industries Committee, also called the Karve Committee, 1955.

mcq.q: According to NCERT, the second phase of the Green Revolution, when HYV technology spread to more states and crops, was roughly:
mcq.why: First phase: about mid-1960s to mid-1970s (Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu; wheat). Second phase: mid-1970s to mid-1980s.

mcq.q: Which of the following correctly gives a sector's share of India's GDP in 1990-91, as per NCERT's table?
options: Industry and services together: 52.5 per cent
mcq.why: 1990-91: agriculture 34.9, industry 24.6, services 40.5 (so industry and services together were 65.1). 59.0 was agriculture's share in 1950-51.

mcq.q:
Consider the following statements about protection under import substitution:
1. A tariff is a tax on imported goods.
2. A quota specifies the quantity of goods that can be imported.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.why: Both are NCERT's definitions of the two forms of protection.

mcq.q:
Consider the following statements about land ceiling:
1. It means fixing the minimum size of land every farmer must own.
2. Land ceiling laws were implemented quickly, without being challenged in courts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.why: Land ceiling fixes the MAXIMUM size of land an individual can own, and big landlords challenged the laws in courts, delaying implementation.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT associated with P.C. Mahalanobis, according to NCERT?
mcq.why: NCERT links Mahalanobis to the ISI, Sankhya and the Second Plan. The 1948 Industrial Policy Resolution isn't credited to him.

mcq.q: Why were some products reserved for small-scale industries?
options: They could not compete with big industrial firms
They were owned and run by the government
They exported most of their production
They used more capital than large firms
mcq.why: NCERT: small-scale industries cannot compete with big firms, so they had to be shielded, including through reservation.

mcq.q:
Consider the following statements about the Green Revolution period:
1. A good proportion of rice and wheat was sold in the market as marketed surplus.
2. As a result, food grain prices rose relative to other items of consumption.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.why: Food grain prices declined (not rose) relative to other items, which benefited low-income groups.

mcq.q: Which public sector bread-making firm does NCERT say was sold to the private sector in 2001?
mcq.why: NCERT's example: Modern Bread, run by the state as if the private sector couldn't make bread, sold to the private sector in 2001. Answer with NCERT's date.

mcq.q:
Consider the following statements about P.C. Mahalanobis:
1. He was born in 1893 in Calcutta.
2. He was made a Fellow of Britain's Royal Society in 1945.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements about planning in India:
1. The idea of five year plans was borrowed from the USA.
2. The long-term plan over twenty years is called the perspective plan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.why: Five year plans were borrowed from the former Soviet Union, the pioneer in national planning; the 20-year plan is the 'perspective plan'.

mcq.q: Which of the following pairs from NCERT's 'match the following' exercise (Exercise 19) is correctly matched?
options: HYV seeds: seeds that give a large proportion of output
Quota: a tax charged on imported goods
Subsidy: tax collected from farmers' produce
GDP: value of all goods imported in one year
mcq.why: HYV seeds give a large proportion of output. A quota is the quantity that can be imported; a subsidy is monetary assistance for production; GDP is the money value of all final goods and services produced in one year.

mcq.q: According to NCERT, a small-scale industrial unit in 1950 was one that invested a maximum of:
mcq.why: ₹5 lakh in 1950; NCERT gives the 'present' limit as ₹1 crore. (Beyond the book: that figure is out of date. Today's MSME limits are far higher and use both investment and turnover.)

mcq.q: The excessive regulation in which licences were misused to block competitors came to be called the:
mcq.why: NCERT: the excessive regulation of what came to be called the permit licence raj prevented certain firms from becoming more efficient.

mcq.q: According to NCERT, serious thought to promoting exports was not given until the:
mcq.why: NCERT: nor was any serious thought given to promote exports until the mid-1980s.

keyPoints: A plan spells out how the resources of a nation should be put to use
It has general goals and specific objectives
To be achieved within a specified period of time
(Optional) In India plans were of five years, an idea borrowed from the former Soviet Union
Goals give the use of a nation's limited resources a clear direction
Clearly specified goals let each plan set priorities, since not every goal can get equal importance
Goals act as a yardstick to check that policies don't contradict them (growth, modernisation, self-reliance, equity)
(Optional) Goals can conflict, e.g. modern technology vs employment, so planners balance them

descriptive.q: What are High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds?
keyPoints: Seeds that give a large proportion of output (high yield)
They led to a large increase in food grain production (the Green Revolution)
Used especially for wheat and rice in the Green Revolution
Need fertiliser, pesticide and regular water in correct proportions
So farmers needed irrigation and money for inputs
Core definition: the portion of agricultural produce that farmers sell in the market (NCERT's text calls it 'marketed surplus'; accept either term)
(Optional, beyond the book) Strictly, marketable surplus is what could be sold: output minus farmers' own consumption, seed, feed and payments in kind
(Optional) Significance: a large marketed surplus during the Green Revolution lowered food grain prices relative to other goods and let the government build buffer stocks

descriptive.q: Why did India opt for planning?
keyPoints: To promote the welfare of all rather than a few
To raise living standards (the First Plan's central objective)
The market alone would leave the great majority behind (distribution by purchasing power)
A mixed economy: the state plans, with the private sector part of the plan effort
Nehru and others sought an alternative to extreme capitalism and socialism: the best features of socialism without its drawbacks; Soviet-style change of ownership wasn't possible in a democracy

descriptive.q: Explain the need and type of land reforms implemented in the agriculture sector.
keyPoints: Land reforms: primarily a change in the ownership of landholdings (text); Exercise 19 calls them improvements in agriculture to raise productivity
Need: intermediaries (zamindars, jagirdars) collected rent without improving land; low productivity; India imported food from the USA
Type 1: abolition of intermediaries, land to the tiller; some 200 lakh tenants came into direct contact with the government, freed from exploitation
Type 2: land ceiling, fixing the maximum land an individual can own
Limits: loopholes, evictions, court delays; success in Kerala and West Bengal

descriptive.q: What is the Green Revolution? Why was it implemented and how did it benefit the farmers? Explain in brief.
keyPoints: Large increase in food grain output from HYV seeds, especially wheat and rice
Needed because productivity was low and agriculture depended on the monsoon
Made India self-sufficient in food grains
Marketed surplus; food prices fell relative to other goods; buffer stocks
Small farmers also gained through low-interest loans, subsidised fertiliser and research institutes

descriptive.q: Explain 'growth with equity' as a planning objective.
keyPoints: Growth alone may not improve how most people live
Benefits must reach the poor, not only the rich
Everyone should meet basic needs: food, a decent house, education and health care
Inequality in the distribution of wealth should be reduced

descriptive.q: Does modernisation as a planning objective create contradiction in the light of employment generation? Explain.
keyPoints: Modernisation means adopting new technology (and a modern social outlook)
Modern technology can raise output but reduce the need for labour
This conflicts with the goal of increasing employment
Planners must balance the goals, which NCERT calls a very difficult job

descriptive.q: Why was it necessary for a developing country like India to follow self-reliance as a planning objective?
keyPoints: Avoid imports of goods India could produce itself, especially food
Reduce dependence on foreign countries
A recently freed nation feared that dependence on imported food, foreign technology and capital would leave its sovereignty vulnerable
Stressed by the first seven five year plans

descriptive.q: What is sectoral composition of an economy? Is it necessary that the service sector should contribute maximum to GDP of an economy? Comment.
keyPoints: Sectoral (structural) composition: the contribution of agriculture, industry and services to GDP
NCERT: in some countries agriculture's growth contributes more to GDP growth, in others the service sector's; India's agriculture share was over 50% at first
Usual path: agriculture declines, industry becomes dominant, then services at higher development
India's change was peculiar: services 40.59% by 1990, ahead of agriculture and industry
So not necessary; it depends on the stage and path of development

descriptive.q: Why was the public sector given a leading role in industrial development during the planning period?
keyPoints: Industrialists lacked capital for big ventures
The market was too small to encourage major projects
Socialist pattern: the state controls the commanding heights (industries vital to the economy)
Private sector policies would complement the public sector

descriptive.q: Explain the statement that the green revolution enabled the government to procure sufficient food grains to build its stocks that could be used during times of shortage.
keyPoints: HYV seeds raised rice and wheat output
A good share was sold as marketed surplus
The government could procure enough grain from the market
Built a buffer stock for times of food shortage

descriptive.q: While subsidies encourage farmers to use new technology, they are a huge burden on government finances. Discuss the usefulness of subsidies in the light of this fact.
keyPoints: Subsidies were needed to encourage adoption of risky new HYV technology, especially by small farmers
Against: purpose served; a substantial share benefits the fertiliser industry and farmers in the more prosperous regions; huge burden on government finances
Prices as signals: subsidised inputs are overused and harm the environment
For: farming is risky and most farmers are poor; removal raises inequality
Balanced view: target subsidies so poor farmers benefit

descriptive.q: Why, despite the implementation of green revolution, 65 per cent of India's population continued to be engaged in the agriculture sector till 1990?
keyPoints: Agriculture's share of GDP fell significantly, but not its share of people (67.5% in 1950 to 64.9% in 1990)
Industrial and service sectors did not absorb workers from agriculture
Output could have grown with fewer workers
Economists call this an important failure of 1950–1990 policies

descriptive.q: Though public sector is very essential for industries, many public sector undertakings incur huge losses and are a drain on the economy's resources. Discuss the usefulness of public sector undertakings in the light of this fact.
keyPoints: Contribution: by 1990 industry became well diversified, largely due to the public sector
Industry's GDP share rose from 13% (1950-51) to 24.6% (1990-91), with about 6% annual growth
Criticism: no distinction between what only the state can do (defence) and what private firms can also do; monopolies kept (telecom waits, Modern Bread, hotels)
Many PSUs made huge losses but kept running, since a government undertaking is hard to close: a drain on limited resources
Counter-view: judge PSUs on welfare, not profits; these conflicts led to the new economic policy of 1991

descriptive.q: Explain how import substitution can protect domestic industry.
keyPoints: Replace imports with domestic production (inward looking trade strategy)
Tariffs: a tax on imports makes them more expensive and discourages their use
Quotas: limit the quantity that can be imported
Domestic firms are shielded from foreign competition while they learn to compete
Also prevented foreign exchange being spent on imports of luxury goods

descriptive.q: Why and how was private sector regulated under the IPR 1956?
keyPoints: Why: socialist pattern of society; state control of the commanding heights
How: three categories of industries (state-only; private supplementing the state; the rest private)
No new industry without a government licence
Licences easier in backward regions, with concessions, for regional equality
Licences needed to expand output or diversify
